# Limits, open questions and directions {#sec-limits}

**Every claim in this book has a boundary, and this chapter states each one
as a fact about the evidence: what is measured, on which split, with which
instrument, and what would move it.** The claims themselves live in the
evidence chapters with their numbers and are not restated here; the thesis
table of the front matter (@sec-verdict) is the list of what is established.
This chapter is the one home for every scope statement in the book. It
reduces each headline claim to its limit, says what the book does not
claim, lists the open questions with the readout that would settle each,
names the datasets that extend the program beyond external aerodynamics,
and ends with the two outcomes that would change the recommendation. Ratios throughout are
baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA; the metric is the area-weighted
relative L2 in float32 (@sec-metrics); protocol: @sec-protocol.

## What this book does not claim {#sec-not-claimed}

**Each claim in this book has a scope, and the list below names what sits
outside it; the sections above state each one with its instrument.**

- **Not that ISLA is more accurate in distribution in general**
  (@sec-limits-in-distribution).
- **Not that equivariance is an accuracy edge in general.** A baseline
  trained in a canonical frame is exactly pose-invariant. ISLA's pose lead
  is against baselines that learn pose from augmentation, in random poses
  (@sec-pose, @sec-pose-contract).
- **Not that discretization consistency is an exact invariance.** It is a
  fine-mesh-limit property: ISLA's residual under a biased draw is
  quadrature variance that shrinks with cell count (@sec-principle,
  @sec-robustness-density).
- **Not that ISLA is indifferent to the training sampling law.** Its
  dependence is weak beside GeoTransolver and Transolver, whose errors
  change by factors. Why the cars show the larger dependence is an open
  question (@sec-training-law).
- **Not that the interior lead is unconditional** (@sec-limits-interior).
- **Not that either architecture extrapolates across a flow regime** or
  transfers zero-shot to a different vehicle family (@sec-limits-regime,
  @sec-limits-transfer).
- **Not that the HiLiftAeroML numbers are test-set numbers**
  (@sec-limits-validation).
- **Not that ISLA's learning curve is always the steeper one.** It is on
  Tensile2d, on the lug and on AirfRANS pressure. On the DrivAerML Surface
  task the two architectures' exponents are the same within the fit, and on
  the fixed-mesh OLBC Poisson set GeoTransolver-512's is the steeper
  (@sec-compute-allocation, @sec-interior-olbc).

## Limits of each headline claim {#sec-review-honesty}

### Surface accuracy, in distribution {#sec-limits-in-distribution}

**The in-distribution lead is against GeoTransolver at its recipe width,
on one dataset, from 109 cars up, and no mechanism for it is claimed.** At
matched parameters (GeoTransolver-512) the two are at parity at 435 cars,
so what ISLA buys at full data is cost rather than accuracy: the same
error with GeoTransolver-512 at 1.17x ISLA's step time and 1.90x its
memory (@tbl-scoreboard-435). Below 109 cars GeoTransolver-256 leads. On
the wings both baselines lead on every rung, and ISLA's width, depth and
learning rate, the cell count and GeoTransolver's width all leave that
ordering where it is (@tbl-wing-controls). What ISLA buys elsewhere is
stated with its scope where it is measured: exact pose covariance
(@sec-pose-contract), weak dependence on the law the training sample is
drawn by (@sec-training-law), slice territories that stay put under a
change of draw (@sec-territories), the interior leads on two datasets
(@sec-interior) and the memory frontier (@sec-review-frontier). What would
move this: a mechanism for the wing deficit, located and removed by a
principled configuration (@sec-open-questions).

### The data-efficiency ladders {#sec-limits-data-efficiency}

**The ladders are data-efficiency measurements over the range of
training-set sizes every production CFD dataset in this program occupies,
not scaling laws.** On the DrivAerML Surface task the flattening has a
measured cause: a shared floor of about 0.040 that both architectures
reach given width and depth, with the cell count flat above 100,000
(@sec-shared-floor). On the wings the flattening is not attributed. Seeds
do not measure the choice of training cases: every seed at a rung trains
on the same curated subset, so a seed range measures initialization, and
the between-draw intervals of @sec-de-controls, three to eleven times
wider at 35 cases, are the uncertainty to read. What would move this: a
ladder whose rungs are each averaged over several training draws.

### The HiLiftAeroML accuracy figures are validation-set figures {#sec-limits-validation}

**Every HiLiftAeroML accuracy number in this book is scored on the shared
180-case validation set on final-epoch checkpoints; no checkpoint is
selected on validation error, but no HiLiftAeroML split remains that
could confirm the numbers independently of the program's own history.**
The validation set entered more than one decision: each architecture's
learning rate on the full split (@sec-lr-protocol), the baselines' rate per
rung, the design of the ablations and the choice of what to present. The
sealed test splits were spent on regime extrapolation and the deflection
split, which between them read every one of the 180 geometries
(results/hilift_exposure_ledger_2026-09-08.json), and because those test
sets cover every geometry (@sec-splits) every remaining test split is held
out per checkpoint but is not a program-level confirmation. What would move
this: a sealed evaluation of the 35-case checkpoints on the 360 test cases
is a within-protocol held-out check of the 35-case ratios; an independent
confirmation needs geometries no part of the program has scored, which on
HiLiftAeroML means a prospective dataset.

### Mechanism: what is known and what is not {#sec-limits-mechanism}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task there is no in-distribution gap left to
explain at the reporting protocol; on the wings the deficit is measured on
every rung and not decomposed.** What the cell count contributes below
the protocol is @sec-equal-budget; the limits on the mechanism are these.

- **No single ingredient of ISLA is load-bearing for its own accuracy,
  as far as it is measured.** The single-factor ablations on the 35-wing
  rung each move the error by a fraction of the
  deficit to the baselines, and the exactness of the covariance contract
  neither costs nor buys anything measurable in distribution at that rung;
  the decomposition is unmeasured at the reporting protocol. What would
  move this: an ablation at the reporting protocol that moves the error by
  the size of the deficit.
- **The measure weights' price is variance plus mesh pattern, and only
  the variance part shrinks with cell count.** Weights off is an ablation
  that prices the measure semantics, never a configuration
  (@sec-principle); the instrument that separates the two parts is the
  training-law test (@sec-training-law), on two datasets.
- **The contracts are exact in float32 and not in bf16.** On the trained
  GPU path the rotation and translation residual is at the level of
  float32 rounding, and at the level of a few percent of the field under
  the bf16 autocast the recipe trains with, mostly ordinary rounding. A
  bf16 deployment does not exercise the contracts at the level the book
  claims for them; float32 inference does (@sec-isla-contracts,
  @sec-using-sampler).

### Regime extrapolation {#sec-limits-regime}

**ISLA's generalization across a physical-regime boundary is measured on
one dataset and one task: on AirfRANS's Reynolds-number and angle-of-attack
extrapolation splits its interior error grows less than
GeoTransolver-volume's on pressure and eddy viscosity and the same on
velocity, and it leads on every field outside the training range
(@sec-interior-extrapolation).** It is unmeasured on the surface task and on
three-dimensional flow. No ISLA lane exists on the HiLiftAeroML sealed
regime splits (angle of attack, attached to separated flow), and the finding
that GeoTransolver and Transolver lose about an order of magnitude across
that boundary is a mechanism finding on those architectures
on those architectures, not a comparison with ISLA. What would move
this: the sealed regime splits run once with ISLA and the unit-direction
baselines at the reporting protocol. A split across geometry *classes*
remains the open test, and none of this book's datasets provides one.

### Interior accuracy {#sec-limits-interior}

**The interior standing of @sec-interior holds at the training query
count on two datasets (DrivAerML Volume task, AirfRANS interior task). ISLA
leads GeoTransolver-volume on velocity on both, leads on pressure on the
cars and trails on pressure and eddy viscosity on the airfoils, every
paired seed ratio on the same side.** Four limits bound it. The comparison is not
resource-matched and the two models do not receive the same inputs.
GeoTransolver-volume fed the physical velocity changes by under 2% on
every field, so the ratios are not an input-scale artifact. The interacting
decode's prediction depends on the joint query set, and training over a
range of counts reduces the dependence without removing it, so the
interacting configuration is deployed at its training count
(@sec-interior-companion). And the
eddy-viscosity metric is on a standardized field, so its ratios are
orderings under that centering, not physical percentages. What would move
this: a third seed of the interior configuration on both datasets, and
GeoTransolver-volume on the 54- and 109-car interior rungs, where only ISLA
is measured (@sec-interior-results).

### The prediction depends on the query set {#sec-limits-query-independence}

**ISLA's prediction at a point depends on which other points are in the
request: every surface point is an interacting token, and so is every
interior query in the reported configuration.** On the interior the
dependence is measured. At the exploration budget a checkpoint trained at
one request size and scored at a fifth of it loses more on every field
than either margin against GeoTransolver-volume. Training over a range of
request sizes reduces that penalty by about 40% at a 3.7% pressure cost
and does not remove it. The queries' routing mass,
a learned fraction of the total boundary measure split over the request,
removes the count scaling of the routing weight by construction, while the
dependence through the shared slices remains (@sec-interior-companion). The
interacting configuration is therefore deployed at its training request
count, and every interior number in the book states that count. The class
has no evaluate-anywhere decode: the request-independent decoder that was
built was several times less accurate on every interior field and was
removed (@sec-arch-passive-decoder). What would move this: a
query-independent decode within seed noise of the interacting one on either
interior dataset.

### Cross-family transfer {#sec-limits-transfer}

**Whether ISLA transfers zero-shot across vehicle families is unmeasured:
no ISLA lane exists for it at any budget, and the finding that
cross-family error is governed by the diversity of the training data is a
mechanism finding on the architectures tested, not
a ranking.** What would move this: a corpus in which geometry, pose, scale
and regime vary one at a time, with ISLA and the unit-direction baselines
trained on it under the protocol.

## Open questions, and what would settle each {#sec-open-questions}

**Each open question carries a readout and, where one has been written, a
preregistered bar; the live status of every item is in @sec-program-status
and the preregistrations are in the notebook.** Unless stated, the readout
is the surface-pressure relative L2 of @sec-metrics and the ratio is
baseline ÷ ISLA, so above one favors ISLA.

| question | what would settle it | bar |
|---|---|---|
| What is the mechanism of the wing deficit? Its location is known: against GeoTransolver-512 the ratio is 0.77 up to 14 degrees and 0.67 from 16 degrees, where the flow separates and both errors double, and the two models rank the cases alike (@sec-de-strata) | the mesher-pattern hypothesis (validation geometries recur in training with a different mesh) tested by a split that holds geometries out entirely at matched case count, at the reporting protocol; the positional hypothesis (GeoTransolver reads absolute position) is quantified by the pose-prior diagnostic (@sec-pose-prior): giving ISLA the dataset's axes, a rejected input, recovers about half of the low-angle gap and a quarter of the high-angle widening, so position in the fixed pose is part of the deficit and the separated regime keeps the rest | the ratio moves toward parity when recurrence is removed, or does not |
| What is ISLA's ratio on the two largest HiLiftAeroML rungs (510 and 1,260 cases)? | ISLA trained there at the reporting protocol | reported as measured |
| Do the 35-case ratios hold on cases no decision has read? | the 35-case ISLA and unit-direction baseline checkpoints scored once on the 360-case sealed test | the validation ratios reproduced within their seed spread |
| Do the capacity floor and the memory frontier reproduce on the wings? On the 510-wing rung the cells and width-independence readings reproduce and the width turnover and the memory frontier do not (@tbl-scalehl) | the width and depth ladders of @sec-shared-floor on a second wing rung at the scaling budget | both ladders flatten at one floor, and the best ISLA at or under each memory budget is at least as accurate as the best GeoTransolver, or not |
| Why does ISLA's training-law dependence differ between datasets (1% on the wings, 8% on the cars)? | the twin training under a third law, or on a third dataset, with the same independent uniform readout (@sec-training-law) | no bar is preregistered; reported as measured |
| Does the architecture match a same-size baseline on a problem that is not external aerodynamics? | a dataset outside external aerodynamics with GeoTransolver trained on it under the fair-comparison protocol (@sec-limits-datasets); the screened-Poisson acceptance case already trains with $K = 0$ global vectors and one global scalar | the error at the level of the same-size baseline on that problem |
| Does either architecture extrapolate across geometry classes? | a split across classes rather than along one parameter of one family | none of this book's datasets provides one |
| Does the interior pressure deficit survive a third seed? | third seeds of the interior configuration at the reporting protocol on both interior datasets | no bar is preregistered; the velocity lead and level eddy viscosity must not move by more than 5% |
| Do the extrapolation splits of AirfRANS (Reynolds number, angle of attack) separate the architectures? | ISLA and GeoTransolver-volume trained on each split, the readout the growth of error from the in-distribution to the extrapolation test set | a 10% difference in error growth counts |

### Datasets beyond external aerodynamics {#sec-limits-datasets}

**The flow standings of this book are measured on external aerodynamics
(DrivAerML, HiLiftAeroML, AirfRANS). Two solids problems (PLAID Tensile2d,
GINOT Bracket Lug), one bracket family under prescribed loads (DeepJEB++)
and two fixed-mesh problems with randomly placed, labeled Dirichlet,
Neumann and Robin segments (the OLBC Poisson and elasticity sets) now carry
standings too (@sec-interior-tensile2d, @sec-interior-lug,
@sec-surface-deepjeb, @sec-interior-olbc). Whether the interface carries to
further steady boundary-driven PDEs is still the open axis.** These sets
were chosen for varying boundary conditions and loads, not only varying
geometry, so that the global-scalar, global-vector and boundary-input
channels are exercised; @sec-datasets-beyond-aero draws each on one sample
and @sec-datasets-detail gives their conversion. On the fixed-mesh sets
GeoTransolver-512 leads by a factor of two to three, and on Tensile2d it
leads at 400 cases: these are the standings that most need a located
mechanism (@sec-interior-olbc). AeroZoo, a diversity-stress aerodynamics
benchmark in generation, is the coming out-of-distribution instance within
external aerodynamics; it carries no number yet, and the status of each
conversion is in @sec-program-status.

## Engineering directions {#sec-future}

**Four directions are engineering, not research: each has a measured
starting point and a stated remainder.**

| direction | what is in place | what remains |
|---|---|---|
| Problems outside external aerodynamics | the interface accepts zero or more global vector inputs and zero or more global scalar inputs, and per-cell boundary data through the boundary-scalar channel (@sec-isla-inputs); the contract tests cover zero and two global directions; a screened-Poisson acceptance case trains with no global vector and one global scalar, and the scalar is decisive where the boundary data cannot substitute for it | a production dataset outside external aerodynamics with a baseline trained on it under the protocol (@sec-limits-datasets) |
| Cost at scale | with the exact fused geometry kernel, the default on CUDA, ISLA's step tracks GeoTransolver's at every token count in about half its memory, and ISLA holds the accuracy-against-memory frontier below about 70 GB at 435 cars (@sec-cost-sweep, @sec-review-frontier) | cost logs for the depth ladder, which reaches the floor at half GeoTransolver's parameters but is absent from the cost frontier; the gap below GeoTransolver's footprint is headroom for a wider or deeper model, since on DrivAerML cells past 100,000 buy nothing |
| Sampling conventions | ISLA's convention-swap penalty converges under refinement, and so does that of GeoTransolver and Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe (ablation); GeoTransolver's and Transolver's as released does not (@sec-consistency-bench) | at 10,000 cells no architecture is consistent across conventions; the fine-mesh limit is within a few percent of reached at 40,000 |
| Query-count consistency of the interior decode | the total query mass is a learned fraction of the total source measure divided by the query count, so neither refining the source nor changing the request size moves the balance between surface and queries (@sec-isla-contracts); count augmentation reduces the interacting decode's dependence without removing it | a decode whose prediction at a point is independent of the request at the interacting configuration's accuracy (@sec-interior-open) |

## What would change the recommendation {#sec-review-roads}

**ISLA is the choice wherever the deployment sampling may differ from the
training sampling, wherever the training sampling law is not the
deployment one, where geometries arrive in arbitrary poses, and where
memory at scale binds, and on the DrivAerML Surface task from about 100
training cars up, where it leads GeoTransolver at its recipe width by up
to 7% in less memory and ties the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512 in
half of it; GeoTransolver is the choice for matched-mesher, known-pose
surface prediction from few training cases on the wings and below about
100 cars (@sec-surface).** The recommendation splits on consistency, and
consistency is a property of the frame, not of the architecture. Every
configuration that centers its coordinates on a statistic of the sampled
points degrades several-fold under a sampling-density bias when the frame
is taken from the biased sample, GeoTransolver and Transolver included.
Only frames that do not read the sample hold: ISLA's origin-free
frame, and the ablations of GeoTransolver and Transolver given
a Horvitz–Thompson center (@sec-robustness-density). Those ablations
locate the property. GeoTransolver and Transolver are stable, in use and
published, and are not modified, so measure weighting and a sample-free
frame reach users through ISLA (@sec-principled-ledger). Two
outcomes would change the recommendation.

**ISLA gains an in-distribution accuracy claim below full data and on the
wings** if the mechanism of the wing deficit is located and removed by a
principled configuration: the geometry-holdout test of
@sec-open-questions is the one such candidate. If the wing deficit
closes, the recommendation on matched-mesher, known-pose surface
prediction from few training cases becomes a trade of a few percent of
accuracy against the contracts rather than a preference for
GeoTransolver.

**The interior recommendation becomes unconditional for ISLA** only if
the AirfRANS pressure and eddy-viscosity deficits close without moving
velocity. Until then the recommendation on the interior is ISLA on
velocity on both datasets and on every DrivAerML Volume field, and
GeoTransolver-volume on AirfRANS pressure and eddy viscosity
(@sec-interior).

If neither fires, the recommendation stands as written, with the bounds
of this chapter attached. The program's ISLA-specific claims are these:
exact covariance and its lead in arbitrary poses; consistency under a
change of inference draw and weak dependence on the training sampling law,
both properties of the origin-free frame and the measure weights; the
interior velocity lead; the cost figures of @sec-capacity; and, on
in-distribution surface accuracy, a lead over GeoTransolver at its recipe
width from about 100 cars up on the DrivAerML Surface task, parity with
the parameter match, and a deficit below 100 cars and on the wings.
